body:
[A10] **Assignment for [A699].** This is release work: milan-fpga #396's gate includes 50 controller-sent soft resets.

Branch `203-aecp-reboot` from main `f65c8ff7`. Implement this issue exactly, as written above:
- **Responses** (IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.43, Figure 7-75):
  - REBOOT to ENTITY descriptor 0 is answered SUCCESS and echoes the command;
  - another descriptor type gets NOT_SUPPORTED;
  - a non-zero index gets NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR;
  - a short command gets BAD_ARGUMENTS;
  - a REBOOT while another controller holds the entity gets ENTITY_ACQUIRED or ENTITY_LOCKED (7.4.1, 7.4.2).
- **ENTITY_DEPARTING** goes out before the request if the entity is advertising. Find and cite the clause in IEEE 1722.1-2021 6.2.1/6.2.6 and Milan v1.2 5.2.
- **`reboot_req_o`** is raised only after the SUCCESS response's transmit-done, and no further command is accepted after it. This is the one authorised top-level port. State in the interface documents whether it is a pulse or a held level. Recommendation: a held level until reset, so the integrator cannot miss it.
- **Docs:** update REQ-FWX-001, GAP-13, the AECP command model and the compliance review entry.
- **Tests and mutants:** a test for every status above, and the mutant that raises the request before the response is sent.

**Parent consumer gate:** work in a committed local clone of milan-fpga dev `1e80128f`, with this head as its gitlink and the new port left unconnected. The parent's reset wiring is milan-fpga #787.

**STOP** if any other top-level port, parameter or register-map change is needed.

[A699] TAKEN
Branch: 203-aecp-reboot from main f65c8ff7c673aaa8e2ea8da654f081ddb13588d8.
Authoritative references: issue #203 body and issuecomment-6493855055; IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.43 (Figure 7-75), 7.4.1, 7.4.2, 6.2.1, 6.2.6; Milan v1.2 5.2; integrator side milan-fpga #787 and #396.
Scope: REBOOT to ENTITY 0 answered SUCCESS echoing the command; NOT_SUPPORTED, NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR, BAD_ARGUMENTS, ENTITY_ACQUIRED / ENTITY_LOCKED; ENTITY_DEPARTING before the request when advertising; reboot_req_o (the one authorised top-level port) raised only after the SUCCESS response's transmit-done, then no further command accepted; REQ-FWX-001, GAP-13, the AECP command model and the compliance review entry; a test per status and the early-request mutant; consumer gate in a committed local scratch clone of milan-fpga dev 1e80128f with this head as the gitlink and the port unconnected.
STOP if any other top-level port, parameter or register-map change is needed.

[A699] REVIEW READY
Head: 1be824fccbda5d3341737f5fe033d60edd27af57 on branch 203-aecp-reboot, from main f65c8ff7c673aaa8e2ea8da654f081ddb13588d8. Nine commits, not pushed. The PR body is prepared with "Closes #203".
Behaviour:
- REBOOT of ENTITY 0 answers SUCCESS, echoing {descriptor_type, descriptor_index} at cdl 16.
- Refusals: another descriptor_type gets NOT_SUPPORTED; ENTITY at a non-zero index gets NO_SUCH_DESCRIPTOR; cdl < 16 gets BAD_ARGUMENTS; under another controller's lock it gets ENTITY_LOCKED.
- ENTITY_ACQUIRED cannot arise, because ACQUIRE_ENTITY is NOT_SUPPORTED (Milan v1.2 5.4.2.1). A test shows it.
- On SUCCESS, in order: the other registered controllers get the unsolicited notification (7.4.43, 7.5.2, Milan v1.2 5.4.5.2); ADP's enable falls (Milan's SHUTDOWN), so ENTITY_DEPARTING goes out where the entity was advertising; then reboot_req_o rises.
- reboot_req_o is a level, held until rst_n, as stated in 02 F02.10 and the integrator guide. It rises only after the SUCCESS response's last byte has left. From that response's grant no further command is accepted.
Clauses:
- ENTITY_DEPARTING: Milan v1.2 5.6.3.3, 5.6.3.5.8, 5.6.3.5.11 and Table 5.51 (5.2 is the chapter overview); IEEE 1722.1-2021 6.2.4.1.3 and 6.2.5.2.2. 6.2.1 introduces the advertising machines and 6.2.6 is the receiving controller's side.
- REBOOT's format is Figure 7-68 (Figure 7-75 is AUTH_ADD_KEY).
Top level: one new output, reboot_req_o. No parameter or register-map change, so no STOP.
Tests: a new section RBT in tb/pp_top, 79 checks, covering every status. 17 rbt-* arms, all KILLED. Among them, rbt-request-at-acceptance (the request raised before the response is sent) is killed by RBT7.
Gates, all rc 0:
- make check; run_suites (1,030,845 checks, 0 failing); check-req-tags (executed); lint_hdl; syn/yosys/run.sh; elab guards.
- Mutant campaigns: aecp_dispatch (5 controls, 86 of 86), aecp 67, d3 110 of 110, notify 137 of 137, ctr 18, acmp 101 of 101, gsi 30, name-wr, elab-guard mutants 160 of 160, aecp_cmds 17 of 17, adp_engine 62.
- The campaigns ran at 5fd298c. Every later commit changes documentation and READMEs only.
Consumer gate: a committed local scratch clone of milan-fpga dev 1e80128f, never pushed, with this head as its gitlink and the port left unconnected.
- Full sweep: 64 suites, 2,191,694 checks, 0 failures. The static, behave, elaboration and documentation gates pass.
- OOC area against dev: -101 LUT, +9 FF.
- Adopting the pin needs four parent edits, listed in the PR body: name the pin at the instance, the behave SERVED row, the feature ledger, and the pin docs.
- The shipping route has 16 slices of headroom, so a route at adoption is the deciding measurement.

[A10] **#203 round 2**: close control-plane transmission after the final ENTITY_DEPARTING

R732-1 is NEGATIVE: https://github.com/Mister-M-alt/protocol-processor-control-plane-avb-milan/pull/209#issuecomment-6503147824. Read it and its probe exactly.

**R732-F1 (MAJOR).** After DEPARTING (cycle 268095) and `reboot_req_o` (268097), three unsolicited LOCK_ENTITY responses go out while the request is held: the automatic-unlock notifications. That breaks acceptance item 3, "no further control-plane transmission after DEPARTING", and the integrator guide's "nothing left to send".

Required:
- After SUCCESS, the notifications to the registered controllers (IEEE 1722.1-2021 7.4.43, 7.5.2) and the final DEPARTING (6.2.6; Milan v1.2 5.6.3.5.8/.11), the processor enters a terminal transmit-quiet state that lasts until reset. It covers every producer: AECP unsolicited and lock expiry, ADP, ACMP, MAAP and SRP. Frame integrity and the held request are kept, and none of the required shutdown frames is suppressed.
- An all-frame assertion runs from the final DEPARTING through a delayed reset. It exercises lock expiry, asynchronous notifications, pending work and the autonomous producers. A planted defect that reopens any one producer or the terminal gate must fail it.
- RBT1 to RBT8 and every round-1 gate stay rc 0.

**R732-F2 (RESIDUE), in this round:** the port comment heading at `protocol_processor_top.sv:823` becomes `REBOOT request (REQ-FWX-001; IEEE 1722.1-2021 §7.4.43; issue #203)`.

Exit: REVIEW READY with the head. The internal review R731 runs at that head.

[A699b] TAKEN
Round 2 (R732-F1, R732-F2) on branch 203-aecp-reboot, adding commits on top of 1be824fccbda5d3341737f5fe033d60edd27af57 (base main f65c8ff7).

[A699b] REVIEW READY
Head: ec1ff275a72d885f0908fd213d8009e9e4dda4d9 on branch 203-aecp-reboot. That is three commits on top of round 1's 1be824fccbda5d3341737f5fe033d60edd27af57 (base main f65c8ff7c673aaa8e2ea8da654f081ddb13588d8). No rebase, not pushed. The PR body is prepared with "Closes #203".
R732-F2: aede92e is comment-only. The heading reads `REBOOT request (REQ-FWX-001; IEEE 1722.1-2021 §7.4.43; issue #203)`; it is line 824, which the review cites as 823.
R732-F1, the terminal transmit-quiet state:
- One gate at the TX arbiter, through which every control-plane frame passes: arb_req_w = arb_want_w & rbt_tx_open_w. From the clock ADP has built and queued its last ENTITY_DEPARTING until rst_n, only ADP's lane is open. ADP's enable has fallen for good, so it builds nothing more, and nothing follows the final DEPARTING.
- The gate only decides which frame starts: no frame is cut, and the held request is unchanged.
- It covers AECP unsolicited (lock expiry, every notification, DEREGISTER), CONTROLLER_AVAILABLE, the listener's probes, MAAP and SRP. ADP is covered by its enable. The answering lanes are closed too.
- It closes only after the DEPARTING is built, not at the SHUTDOWN. A producer held at the gate keeps its shared TX slot (the originator's timer arms only at the serializer), so a gate closed at the SHUTDOWN can leave ADP no slot. Then no DEPARTING and no request come: RBT11 shows the deadlock.
- The SUCCESS response, the notifications and the DEPARTINGs are all still sent.
Tests: section RBT has 127 checks, 0 failures (RBT1 to RBT8 kept).
- RBT9 is the all-frame assertion from the final DEPARTING through a reset withheld 75 s. Lock expiry, AVB-info/path/grandmaster/counter changes, a queued command and later commands, a bound sink with a discovered talker, internal MAAP, SRP and a link bounce are all live. The MAC holds the DEPARTING's last byte 1.5 s first. No byte is offered on tx_* until the reset. The unsolicited AECP lane, the listener, MAAP and SRP each asked to send. After the reset the entity advertises again.
- RBT10 does the same for CONTROLLER_AVAILABLE in its own 65 s window.
- RBT11 takes every TX slot at the SHUTDOWN; the DEPARTING and the request still follow.
Arms: 13 new gate arms, all KILLED by name. They drop the gate, close it only with the request, let each producer through (notifications, originator, listener, MAAP, SRP), re-enable ADP, let each answering lane through with its command gates dropped, close the gate at the SHUTDOWN, and close it on the DEPARTING or the notifications. rbt-rx-gate-dropped and rbt-engine-hold-dropped keep their plants and are named by RBT7 and by the engine's command count, because RBT6's late answers now reach no wire. All 30 REBOOT counts equal their README cells.
Gates at the head, all rc 0:
- make check; run_suites (1,030,893 checks, 0 failing); check-req-tags (executed, 262 lines); lint_hdl (5.052, 5.050); syn/yosys/run.sh; elab guards 93.
- Mutant campaigns: aecp_dispatch (5 controls, 99 of 99), aecp 67, d3 110 of 110 (two parts, reconciled), notify 137 of 137, ctr 18, acmp 101 of 101, gsi 30, name-wr, elab-guard mutants 160 of 160, aecp_cmds 17 of 17, adp_engine 62.
Consumer gate: the scratch parent (local clone of milan-fpga dev 1e80128f, never pushed), pinned to this head with the port left unconnected.
- Full sweep: 64 suites, each once, 2,191,694 checks, 0 in-suite failures. The first run's shards shared CPUs with the campaigns and hit the wall clock, so each shard was re-run whole with SUITE_TIMEOUT=7200.
- 38 static, behave, elaboration and documentation gates pass.
- OOC area against dev: -257 LUT, +9 FF.
- No new adoption step beyond round 1's four.
- No top-level port, parameter or register-map change in this round, so no STOP.
